name: United States
sources: No per-nation sourcing note existed when this nation was first entered in init.rs; the table header recorded only "Transcribed-not-invented: approximate 1990 historical starting conditions".
Figures below are transcribed unchanged from that table. Their origin was not documented at the time and is a known gap in provenance.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.9155%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series USA (United States): 235,825,000 in 1984 to 246,819,000 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

reserves_bn = 168.584 ($bn). Total reserves including gold, USA, 1989: US$168583563269.38 (World Bank World Development Indicators series FI.RES.TOTL.CD, 'Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)', retrieved from the World Bank API on 2026-09-02; indicator lastupdated 2026-07-13). THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. LIMIT STATED: this series is official reserve assets. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 40 were held and are listed below with their citations; 8 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): comp_risc_superscalar, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_conjugate_vaccine, tran_high_speed_rail, agri_protected_cultivation, agri_tissue_culture_propagation, agri_marine_aquaculture.

granted.source: Route (a) production. Intel's 80486 shipped on a 1.0-micron CHMOS process from April 1989 - the registry entry's own citation - and US fabs were in the 1-Mbit and 4-Mbit DRAM generations by 1989: CIA SW 89-10032 (1989) records that 'the West is manufacturing second-generation VLSI devices (that is 4-megabit memories) in volume'. Corroboration for use: World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 21.50 PCs per 100 people, the highest value in the series.

The NSFNET T1 backbone came online in 1988 and the ARPANET was decommissioned in 1990, the NSFNET backbone carrying the traffic it had proved could be carried - the deployment this node's own source comment reads its floor from (spheres-sim/src/tech/mod.rs, core_packet_internetworking comment). A domestically built, domestically routed IP backbone with domestic hosts, by definition.

AT&T supplied one of the three separately-contracted subsegments of TAT-8, the first fibre-optic cable across an ocean, which entered service on 14 December 1988: 6,700 km, two working fibre pairs plus a spare, 120 submerged regenerators, 295.6 Mbit/s per fibre. Supplying a repeatered transoceanic single-mode system is proof of the full conjunction - fibre, lasers, repeaters and line terminals. Corning's single-mode fibre and AT&T's own fibre production stand behind it.

Hercules (Magnamite AS4/IM7, Magna, Utah), Amoco Performance Products (Thornel) and BASF Structural Materials (Celion, the former Celanese line) all ran PAN carbon-fibre plants through the 1980s; the AV-8B wing, this node's own citation, entered USMC service in January 1985 on domestic fibre.

Combined-cycle plant has been in commercial operation in the United States since the GE STAG (STeam And Gas) product line of 1968; Jersey Central Power & Light's Gilbert Generating Station, Milford NJ, is the station generally cited as the first US commercial combined-cycle plant (STAG unit, early 1970s). The airtight later case is the Cool Water Coal Gasification Program at Daggett, California - a 120 MWe integrated gasification combined-cycle plant built by Southern California Edison with Texaco, EPRI and GE, which ran from May 1984 to January 1989. The tree's own comment records that GE's Frame 7F entered commercial service in 1990; that first machine went to a US station (Virginia Power's Chesterfield), which presupposes a US combined-cycle industry already in place on 1 January 1990.

PCR was conceived and commercialised in the United States: Kary Mullis conceived it at Cetus Corporation, Emeryville, California in 1983, and Cetus shipped Taq polymerase and the first thermal cycler in 1987 — the node's own citation, and the moment it became a method rather than a result. Science named Taq polymerase its Molecule of the Year in 1989, the first year that award was given. American laboratories were the instrument's first and largest market.

The entry's own citation: Intel began volume production of the 80386 in June 1986 and Compaq shipped the Deskpro 386 in September 1986. World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 21.50 PCs per 100 people, the highest in the series and 8.8x the World value.

The entry's own citation: Oracle shipped the first commercial relational DBMS in 1979 and IBM put DB2 on MVS in 1983 - both American products in American institutional use throughout the 1980s. Oracle's restated 1990 revenue was $916m.

AT&T's 5ESS digital exchange entered service in 1982 and SS7 common-channel signalling was carrying the US network by the late 1980s - the deployment this node's own source comment reads its 1990 floor from (spheres-sim/src/tech/communications.rs, comm_digital_switching comment). Cross-checked by R3: AMPS commercial service in Chicago from October 1983.

Sprint finished cutting the last of its traffic off copper in May 1988 and was the first carrier anywhere that was one hundred percent digital fibre; AT&T and MCI followed in the early nineties. This is the deployment this node's own source comment reads its floor from (spheres-sim/src/tech/communications.rs, comm_fibre_optic_backbone comment).

US industry was the world's principal builder of geostationary communications satellites through the 1980s: Ford Aerospace built the Intelsat V series and Hughes Aircraft the Intelsat VI series and the HS-376 bus - the very satellites this node's own source comment names as carrying the long-haul traffic by 1990 ('the Intelsat V and VI series', spheres-sim/src/tech/communications.rs). Hughes was also the long-time subcontractor partner on the Canadian Anik programme.

AMPS commercial cellular service opened in Chicago in October 1983 - the deployment this node's own source comment reads its floor from (spheres-sim/src/tech/communications.rs, comm_cellular_analogue comment: 'AMPS in Chicago from October 1983'). World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 5,283,055 US mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990, the largest in the world.

Exxon Production Research shot the first three-dimensional seismic survey in 1967 as a pilot, and the first commercial 3-D surveys followed in the Gulf of Mexico in the 1970s. By the late 1980s 3-D was standard practice for Gulf of Mexico field development rather than a special case, and the entire 3-D acquisition and processing contracting industry - Geophysical Service Inc., Western Geophysical, Seiscom Delta - was American with the Gulf as its principal market. The registry's own comment ('a hundred-odd surveys had been shot by the late 1980s') is describing, in the main, surveys shot over US acreage.

The Austin Chalk horizontal campaign in Texas, 1986-1990 - the registry's own cited exemplar ('the Austin Chalk campaign of 1986-90 proved it paid'). Oryx Energy and others drilled and produced hundreds of horizontal wells into the fractured chalk through the second half of the 1980s, and it is the campaign that turned horizontal drilling from a technical demonstration into an economic method. Wells drilled under that campaign were producing on 1 January 1990.

The Carrisa Plain photovoltaic plant in San Luis Obispo County, California - ARCO Solar, 5.2 MW of crystalline-silicon modules on trackers, built in stages 1983-1985 and the largest photovoltaic plant in the world when completed. The Sacramento Municipal Utility District's 1 MW PV1 array beside Rancho Seco followed in 1984. ARCO Solar was the world's largest module manufacturer through the 1980s. Installed, generating, and at a scale nobody else matched.

Intel's 80486, 1.2 million transistors on a 1.0-micron CMOS process, was announced in April 1989 and shipping during 1989 - the same device the registry's core_cmos_submicron comment cites - and IBM, Texas Instruments, Motorola and Micron were in 4 Mb DRAM or equivalent production.
The AV-8B Harrier II's one-piece carbon-fibre wing, built by McDonnell Douglas, in USMC service from January 1985 - this node's own citation.

Unimation's Unimate went to work at GM's Trenton plant in 1961 - this node's own citation - Cincinnati Milacron's T3 of 1974 was the first computer-controlled industrial robot, and Adept Technology, founded 1983, built direct-drive arms and their controllers. Noted for accuracy: by 1 January 1990 Unimation had passed to Staubli (1989) and Milacron's robot line went to ABB during 1990; Adept remained American.

NUMMI, the Toyota / GM joint venture at Fremont, began production in December 1984 running TPS with a UAW workforce in a plant GM had closed - this node's own citation - and Toyota's wholly owned Georgetown, Kentucky plant followed in May 1988. American-managed adoption is separately attestable: Harley-Davidson's Materials As Needed programme from 1982, and the just-in-time conversions at Omark Industries and Hewlett-Packard in the same period.

Pratt & Whitney's PWA 1480 entered commercial service in the JT9D-7R4 in September 1982, the first structural use of a single crystal anywhere - this node's own citation - with GE's Rene N4 / N5 following and Howmet and Precision Castparts casting them.

Croat's melt-spun NdFeB at General Motors, with the Magnequench plant at Anderson, Indiana from 1986 (bonded), and sintered production at Crucible / Hitachi Magnetics in Michigan; the operational use is the voice-coil motors of American hard-disk drives - Seagate, Conner, Maxtor.

3D Systems of Valencia, California shipped the SLA-1, the first commercial stereolithography machine, in 1988, on Charles Hull's patent granted 11 March 1986 - this node's own citation - and DuPont's Somos line followed at the end of the decade with its own photopolymer chemistry, so both legs of the question, machine and resin, sit on domestic ground.

Texas Instruments Paveway semi-active laser guidance: Paveway I in combat over North Vietnam from 1968 and against the Thanh Hoa bridge on 13 May 1972; Paveway II and III in series production through the 1980s. Rockwell AGM-114A Hellfire, semi-active laser seeker, initial operational capability with the AH-64A in 1984. Martin Marietta M712 Copperhead 155 mm semi-active laser guided artillery projectile, fielded 1984.

Hughes AN/APG-63 pulse-Doppler look-down/shoot-down radar in the F-15A, in USAF service from January 1976; Westinghouse AN/APG-68 in the F-16C from 1986; RCA AN/SPY-1A passive phased array at sea in USS Ticonderoga (CG-47), commissioned 22 January 1983.

Lockheed F-117A Nighthawk: initial operational capability October 1983 with the 4450th Tactical Group, first combat over Panama in Operation Just Cause, 20 December 1989. Northrop B-2A rolled out 22 November 1988 and first flew 17 July 1989. Shaping, radar-absorbent material and the RCS measurement ranges are all domestic.

USS San Juan (SSN-751), first of the Improved Los Angeles (688i) class, commissioned 6 August 1988 — the class that introduced the quieting improvements the node cites. Preceded by the Ohio-class SSBN, lead boat commissioned 11 November 1981, with rafted machinery and anechoic coating.

KH-11 KENNEN, first launched 19 December 1976 — the first US reconnaissance satellite to return its imagery by radio downlink rather than by recovered film capsule, with successive vehicles operational throughout the 1980s.

Three named recombinant protein drugs in American clinical use before 1990: Humulin, recombinant human insulin (Genentech/Eli Lilly), approved by the FDA on 30 October 1982 — the first drug made by a genetically engineered organism, and the node's own citation; Protropin, recombinant human growth hormone (Genentech), approved 1985; and Epogen, epoetin alfa (Amgen), approved 1 June 1989.

WHO/UNICEF WUENIC estimate of DTP3 coverage among one-year-olds, United States, 1990: 90% — at or above the WHO Universal Childhood Immunization 1990 target of 80%. Series: WUENIC DTP3 (dtp3.csv, row 'United States,USA,1990,90').

Grant rests on the MRI-and-conventional-CT half, not on helical CT. FONAR of Melville, New York shipped the first commercial MRI scanner in 1980, and General Electric Medical Systems introduced its Signa 1.5-tesla superconducting MRI in the mid-1980s; computed tomography had been standard equipment in American hospitals since the second half of the 1970s. Both modalities were designed, manufactured and operated in the United States a decade before the start date.

Orthoclone OKT3 (muromonab-CD3, Ortho Pharmaceutical), approved by the FDA in 1986 for acute renal-allograft rejection — the node's own citation, the first therapeutic monoclonal antibody approved anywhere, and on 1 January 1990 still the only one. It was in routine use in American transplant units through the late 1980s.

The four-dye fluorescent method was published from Leroy Hood's laboratory at Caltech in Nature in 1986 (Smith, Hunkapiller and colleagues), and Applied Biosystems of Foster City shipped the 370A on it in 1987 — the node's own citation. American genome and molecular-biology laboratories were the instrument's first market, two to three years before the start date.

Double-stack rail transport was invented in the United States: the first all-double-stack train left Los Angeles for South Kearny, New Jersey in 1984 (APL/Southern Pacific), and double-stack well cars were standard US intermodal practice on multiple railroads by 1990. Wikipedia, 'Double-stack rail transport' (country list: United States 1984, China 2018, Kenya 2018, Brazil 2019; no European operation). The registry entry's own comment dates the first APL train to 30 March 1984.

American President Lines' C-10 class, lead ship President Truman, delivered 1988 at 4,500 TEU with a 129 ft (39.3 m) beam - the first containership class to exceed the Panama Canal's 32.2 m width limit. Built by German yards, owned and operated by APL of Oakland, California, in US-flag transpacific service; six ships were commissioned. The Geography of Transport Systems, 'Evolution of Containerships'; Maritime Reporter, October 1988, 'Two More C-10 Containerships Delivered To APL By German Yards'; globalsecurity.org, 'President Truman C10-M-F150a'.

US Customs' Automated Broker Interface (ABI), a component of the Automated Commercial System, has allowed brokers and importers to file entry data with Customs electronically since its implementation in 1984; ABI is codified at 19 CFR Part 143 Subpart A. US domestic EDI ran on ANSI ASC X12 rather than EDIFACT, which is why the standard applied here reads 'a standard syntax' rather than 'UN/EDIFACT specifically'.

Micro-irrigation reached about 1.5 million acres (~600,000 ha) in the United States by 1990, concentrated on California and Florida permanent and vegetable crops - Workforce LibreTexts, Irrigation Systems Management (AET 021), 14.2 'Microirrigation: History and Impact', reporting the 1991-era worldwide micro-irrigation estimates. The tree's own entry comment names 'the American southwest' as one of the two deployments its 1990 floor is read off (spheres-sim/src/tech/agriculture.rs:45-49).

John Cadotte's FT-30 thin-film composite polyamide chemistry was developed and commercialised at FilmTec in Minneapolis at the turn of the 1980s - the deployment the tree's own entry comment reads its floor off (spheres-sim/src/tech/agriculture.rs:55-59) - and FilmTec was bought by Dow in 1985, supplying the domestic market through the decade. Separately, Orange County Water District's Water Factory 21 had run reverse osmosis on treated municipal wastewater for injection into the Talbert Gap seawater barrier since 1976-77, the first plant in the world to purify wastewater to drinking standards by RO (OCWD history; California Water Environment Association, 'Water Factory 21 - The Legacy Remains'). LIMIT STATED: WF-21's original 5 mgd train was cellulose acetate, so the COMPOSITE half of this cell rests on FilmTec's domestic manufacture and supply, not on WF-21's first elements.

CTIC National Crop Residue Management Survey: 53.3 million acres - 19% of US cropland - under conservation tillage in 1990. The survey has been compiled annually since 1982 and is the only US survey measuring and tracking tillage type by crop at county level (Conservation Technology Information Center, Crop Residue Management Survey).

The USDA/NSF/EPA 'Huffaker Project' - Principles, Strategies and Tactics of Pest Population Regulation and Control in Major Crop Ecosystems, led by Carl B. Huffaker - ran from 1972 to 1978 across eighteen universities and put integrated pest management into US cotton, alfalfa, soybean, citrus, pome and stone fruit and pine systems, and IPM has been a funded USDA Extension Service programme since the 1970s.

FGD systems emerged on US coal-fired power plants and industrial processes in the early 1970s, alongside Japan, and a scrubber fleet was in service under the New Source Performance Standards well before 1990 (Nature Communications 11 (2020), 'Diffusion of flue gas desulfurization...'). STATED EXPLICITLY so the cell cannot be misread: this grant does NOT rest on Title IV of the 1990 Clean Air Act Amendments, which is after the start date and whose phase I bound 110 power stations only from January 1995 (spheres-sim/src/tech/agriculture.rs:167-172).
